ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute: the fare was a fixed RydeX quote and the only off-route movement was covered by the rider's prior in-app consent; no fare adjustment and no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is route_deviation, not safety. safety_concern = none.

Fare model (RD-0/RD-2): RydeX is a fixed-quote service — total charged $23.18 (base 3.90 + distance 13.88 + time 3.93 + platform 1.47). Distance changes do not change the fare. There are no tolls/ERP, no waiting fee, no edit-destination fee and no manual add-ons in the breakdown, so even on the route-deviation branch there is nothing monetary to refund; RD-2 non-metered branch would yield $0.00 → no_action.

Route: GPS (5 s samples, thinned to 30 s) shows the vehicle leaving the quoted corridor after ~10:02 (quoted polyline runs Punggol Rd → TPE; trace instead goes via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive area, ~1.3945/103.9069 at 10:02:50, before rejoining the TPE corridor near 1.3931/103.9132 at 10:06:20). That is one off-route segment (seg1, ~0.8–1.0 km extra).

RD-5 consent: at 10:01:10, i.e. before the vehicle left the corridor, the driver asked "Jam on Tampines Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1?" and the rider replied "Sure, no problem." at 10:01:50. This is a rider-authored message, sent before the deviation began, agreeing to a specific named route. I tried to falsify it and cannot: (i) the location of the diversion at 10:02:50 (1.3945, 103.9069) is exactly the Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 area, i.e. the record does tie the driven segment to the named road, satisfying G13's correspondence requirement; there is no later stop or message naming a different road or place. Consent is therefore established and covers this segment. RD-4 is not relied on for the exemption (no LTA incident on the route; the TPE band-2 record can only corroborate, and RD-4(b) does not exempt alone), and the driver's statement is not used as proof of the rider's verbal agreement — the chat alone suffices.

Because the only off-route segment is covered by prior consent, there is no unexempted segment under RD-1, so RD-2 produces no refund. RD-6 is not triggered (refund not > 0 and no RD-1 violation recorded; driver's 90-day route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 anyway). Profile facts did not decide anything.

Evidence status: sufficient for the elements relied on (timed chat, complete GPS trace, fare breakdown). The deviation magnitude (extra_km) is not precisely derivable from the thinned 30 s trace and the route is a synthetic loop in the polyline data, so confidence is set at 0.6; the outcome is insensitive to it because the fare is fixed and consent covers the segment.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route movement from ~10:02 to ~10:06 via Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 before rejoining the TPE corridor. The driver asked before turning off (10:01:10) and the rider expressly agreed (10:01:50), a rider-authored message sent before the segment began; the agreed named road matches where the trace actually went (1.3945, 103.9069 at 10:02:50), satisfying RD-5's correspondence requirement and G13. Exempt under RD-5; the fixed RydeX quote is unaffected in any event (RD-2).

rejected_claims.reason: There was one off-route segment, but it was expressly agreed by the rider in-app before it began (RD-5), and the RydeX fare is a fixed quote unaffected by distance (RD-2 non-metered branch), so no refund is due.
No traffic-incident fact on the replaced optimal route and the TPE band-2 record alone cannot exempt (RD-4(a)/(b)); the exemption rests on the rider's consent, not on traffic.
